In Switzerland, the Old Age and Survivors' Insurance (AHV) is mandatory for all residents aged 18 or older, regardless of their employment status, as long as they are considered resident in Switzerland. This applies to both working individuals and those who are not currently working or receiving income. Contributions are typically deducted from wages or salaries, but non-workers (e.g., retirees, stay-at-home individuals, or those receiving other forms of income) are still required to make contributions if they have an income subject to AHV contribution or are otherwise obligated under the law. Exceptions may exist for certain categories of individuals, such as foreign residents with specific visa statuses, but generally, the rule is that all Swiss residents aged 18 or older must pay AHV contributions.
